executiveSummary: Analysis of 20 surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning November 2025 through May 2026 reveals a complex multi-threat landscape across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) continues to circulate in the Americas with ongoing animal-to-human spillover risk, representing a critical zoonotic threat requiring heightened surveillance. Concurrent alerts for Mpox, Yellow Fever, Dengue, and Measles indicate sustained arboviral and vaccine-preventable disease pressure across the Americas region. Respiratory pathogen co-circulation including seasonal influenza, RSV, and pertussis resurgence compounds the public health burden entering mid-2026.
bottomLine: Multiple simultaneous disease threats across the Americas and Europe—led by H5N1 zoonotic spillover risk and arboviral surges—demand coordinated cross-regional surveillance and response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates in Nov 2025 and Mar 2026 indicating ongoing H5N1 activity in the Americas
Animal-to-human spillover risk with documented cases in the Americas region
Sustained circulation in avian and mammalian hosts raising pandemic preparedness concerns
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interface; reinforce PPE protocols for exposed workers; accelerate H5N1 vaccine candidate readiness and antiviral stockpiling

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 23 2026 indicating active Mpox transmission in the Americas
Ongoing circulation following the 2022-2024 global emergency period
Risk of clade differentiation and spread to vulnerable populations
threats.action: Strengthen contact tracing and ring vaccination programs; ensure diagnostic capacity for clade differentiation; monitor for unusual clinical presentations

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 13 2026 indicating active yellow fever activity
Epizootics in non-human primates serving as early warning signals
Risk to unvaccinated travelers and populations in transitional zones
threats.action: Intensify vaccination campaigns in at-risk departments and municipalities; enhance entomological surveillance; ensure alert systems for epizootic events in non-human primates

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 18 2026 documenting elevated dengue activity across the Americas
Historically high case counts consistent with recent record-breaking seasons
Multiple serotypes co-circulating increasing severe disease risk
threats.action: Scale up vector control operations; expand dengue case management capacity; monitor for serotype shifts that may increase hemorrhagic fever risk

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Dual PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained resurgence
Increased incidence observed across multiple countries in the Americas
Infant mortality risk elevated in under-vaccinated populations
threats.action: Review and strengthen infant vaccination schedules; implement maternal Tdap immunization programs; enhance laboratory confirmation capacity across the region

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 3 2026 indicating measles activity in the Americas
Risk of importation and spread in populations with vaccination gaps
Americas region previously certified measles-free faces re-establishment risk
threats.action: Conduct rapid vaccination coverage assessments; implement supplementary immunization activities in low-coverage areas; strengthen airport and border point surveillance

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV Co-circulation
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alert January 2026 on simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation
April 2026 PAHO alert marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
ECDC weekly threat reports throughout April-May 2026 tracking respiratory pathogens in Europe
threats.action: Ensure influenza vaccine deployment ahead of Southern Hemisphere peak season; reinforce hospital surge capacity for respiratory illness; monitor for unusual influenza strains

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 10 2026 indicating chikungunya activity
Aedes mosquito vector shared with dengue amplifies concurrent transmission risk
Risk of geographic expansion into previously unaffected areas
threats.action: Integrate chikungunya surveillance into existing arboviral monitoring systems; strengthen vector control; ensure clinical differentiation from dengue in case management protocols

selectAgentSummary: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) is classified as a BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential. Two PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025 and March 2026) document ongoing H5N1 activity in the Americas, including animal reservoirs and spillover risk to humans. This represents the highest-priority select agent signal in the current surveillance dataset. Yellow Fever virus, also a BSL-3 select agent, has triggered a PAHO epidemiological alert in March 2026 for the Americas region. Hantavirus, a BSL-3 agent, was flagged in a December 2025 PAHO alert for Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome in the Americas. These three BSL-3 pathogens require strict containment protocols, enhanced diagnostic biosafety measures, and coordinated international reporting.
amrSignals: No explicit AMR reports identified in current surveillance dataset; Bordetella pertussis resurgence warrants monitoring for macrolide treatment failures; H5N1 antiviral resistance surveillance recommended given widespread oseltamivir use in exposed populations
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen alert burden across the Americas suggests systemic surveillance system stress and potential diagnostic resource competition
Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset in April 2026 coinciding with active arboviral and respiratory co-circulation creates compound healthcare system pressure
Recurrence of pertussis resurgence signals across two consecutive PAHO reporting periods indicates potential waning immunity or vaccination coverage gaps requiring structural intervention
H5N1 persistence across two PAHO reporting cycles spanning November 2025 to March 2026 indicates enzootic establishment rather than transient incursion in parts of the Americas
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert from PAHO (February 2026) signals emerging non-communicable pharmaceutical risk intersecting with communicable disease surveillance frameworks
